The nephron is part of the urinary syste.why: Almost never stated: the nephron is described as the unit of the kidney, and the kidney as an organ of the urinary system. No exact form of the fact was found, while 'nephron(s)' near 'kidney' is about 70 times as frequent as near 'urinary system', and the sampled 'urinary system' hits list the kidney's parts inside a description of the system. It follows from the two premises by transitivity of 'part of'.

notes: Mirrors biology-replace-0015: deletes 'The nephron is part of the urinary system.' Each world forgets one premise. The premise-route and transitivity queries are rephrased around the original system and are does-not-know in both worlds. Side facts listed so that no route goes around the forgotten premise: in w1 the model forgets where the nephron's parts (the glomerulus, the tubules) are, since 'glomeruli are in the kidney' would otherwise reach the urinary system; in w2 it forgets the kidney's grouping with the ureters and bladder. Doubt: a model might still reason from function (the kidneys make urine) to the urinary system in w2; the world asks that this grouping go with the premise.
